item.title: Military Education Benefits: DOD Should Take Steps to Ensure Service Members Receive Information About Tuition Assistance
item.description:
What GAO Found
When service members move to a new base, the Department of Defense (DOD) requires that the military services provide information about educational benefits, including tuition assistance, during orientation.
However, GAO reviewed the education and orientation policies and practices for the military services and found that two of the services—the Navy and Air Force—do not require their military bases to provide information on education, including tuition assistance information, as part of orientation for newly assigned service members. Officials from the DOD office that oversees educational benefit programs said they encourage the services to provide tuition assistance information at orientation, but they do not enforce the policy because they consider it a guideline rather than a requirement. However, the policy states that each military service “will provide” this information as part of its orientation to each new DOD base. Service members in discussion groups and officials GAO interviewed said that some service members were not aware of the tuition assistance benefit. If DOD ensures that all the services provide the information at orientation in accordance with its policy, the department can deliver equal access to information about this important and valuable benefit.
Statements from DOD Service Members about Awareness of Tuition Assistance
Note: Quotes from service members have been edited for brevity and clarity.
The services promote tuition assistance to service members using other methods besides orientation, such as one-on-one counseling and informal conversations. These methods are mostly directed at those who are already aware of tuition assistance.
Service member participation in tuition assistance decreased in all but one of the military services from fiscal year 2015 through fiscal year 2024, the most recent year that data were available. While the Marine Corps experienced a 3 percent increase in participation, the Army, Navy and Air Force saw declines ranging from 1 to 6 percent. Marine Corps officials attributed their increase to leadership support for expanded program access, including no longer requiring service members to serve 2 years before being eligible. Officials from the other services said participation declines might have occurred for various reasons, including requirements for service members to serve a certain number of years before being eligible and decreased funding.
Why GAO Did This Study
Many young people want to join the military for the education benefits it offers, according to a spring 2025 DOD survey. The tuition assistance program provides funding for eligible active-duty service members to pursue education in their off-duty hours.
The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 authorized approximately $434 million for DOD tuition assistance and other voluntary education programs for the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, and Air Force.
House Report 118-529 includes a provision for GAO to review active-duty service members’ awareness of tuition assistance. This report examines, among other things, to what extent active-duty service members receive information about tuition assistance and how participation in the program has changed.
GAO (1) analyzed summary information on program participation from fiscal year 2015 through fiscal year 2024; (2) reviewed relevant federal laws and budget documents; (3) analyzed the extent to which the services’ tuition assistance policies and practices are consistent with DOD’s policy; (4) conducted four site visits and held 10 discussion groups with a total of 112 active-duty service members; and (5) interviewed DOD and service officials and military education counselors.
